subject: Banking
title: How Banks Use Leverage
description: A fast breakdown of How Banks Use Leverage for builders.

hook.text: Banks hold $10-12 in assets for every $1 of their own money.

buildup.text: A 1% return on $1 trillion in assets equals $10 billion.

discovery.text: Leverage is why banking seems so profitable. Small margins on borrowed money create big returns for shareholders.

twist.text: Leverage also means a 10% loss in asset values wipes out all equity.

climax.text: Leverage makes banking the world's most rewarding and most dangerous business.

punchline.text: $10 borrowed for every $1 owned. Leverage makes banks rich and fragile.

quiz.question: What does 10:1 leverage mean for a bank?
options: The bank holds $10 in assets for every $1 of its own capital
